about: Declared differences (APP-DESIGN §7.3): each mask names the element that may differ, the screens it applies to, the rectangle it covers in tC4's screenshot of each, and the ruling it cites (`build`, or an owner ruling that docs/DIFFERENCES.md lists under "Where the rebuild differs from tC4 4.0 on purpose"). `target` is tC4's element; `rust` is the rebuild's when it differs, null meaning the same as `target`; `<OBS>` and `<BIBLE>` stand for the two projects. `meaning` lists the values of what the DOM shows that may differ, as [tC4, rebuild] pairs. Rectangles are measured on tC4 by measure-masks.mjs on the baseline's machine; the gate fails a capture whose masked element lies outside its rectangle. `rustAbsent` says why the rebuild has no such element on these screens yet: the mask then takes tC4's element out alone, the rest of the row's difference is a residual's, and the gate fails once the rebuild draws the element.

masks.why: The line names the program that runs: tC4 4.0.0-rc.2 (d25b787) there, the rebuild's own version and build here.
The attachment names the program and the platform that send the report: tC4's build and Linux x86_64 there, the rebuild's own here.

The rebuild syncs OBS projects, so the shared OBS card reads "Sync with Door43" where tC4 reads "Upload changes". The longer label also moves the element: it is 148 px wide and 15 px lower in the Rust page, so the rectangle covers both. Since E2 the card also carries "Receive work from a file", which put the Rust element at x 658, y 277 (147 by 31); E2 step 7 folded that into one "Save or receive work by USB" menu, which moves it to x 630 (147 by 31). The rectangle covers tC4's place and the Rust one.

The rebuild opens private repositories after sign-in, so its note has no sentence that only public repositories can be opened; a new key, openDoor43.whereAny, replaces openDoor43.where. tC4's note has no test id; the rebuild's note starts with the same words, so the one text target finds it on both sides (B9b). Each rectangle is widened to hold the rebuild's line too: without the project name field (ruling H14, E1c) the dialog is shorter and its centred box sits lower.

tC4's refusal says to make sure that the repository is public; the rebuild opens private repositories, so its sentence must not say this (Q-21: openDoor43.refused.notOpened). The rectangle covers the sentence on both sides: the rebuild's dialog sits half a line higher, by Q3's shorter note (B9b). Each rectangle is widened to hold the rebuild's line too: without the project name field (ruling H14, E1c) the dialog is shorter and its centred box sits lower.

target.text: tC4 could not get the project from Door43.

masks.why: The line names the Door43 server the build signs in to (tC4's dcsServer rule, #120): git.door43.org in tC4's capture, the loopback test Door43 tc4 serve was started with in the rebuild's, so that nothing leaves the machine.

The date of the version saved on this computer is when the capture run saved it, so it is the run's clock in each capture (tC4's gallery shows its own capture's). The version on top is Mine in the rebuild and Teammate 2 in tC4, both dated at the same place.
